//: R9 (Y8) — what each published subpath weighs, and what it is supposed to weigh.
`distBytes` is the gate `src/weight.test.ts` enforces: the summed bytes of the `dist/`
files an entry transitively reaches. It needs no bundler and no network, so it is the
same number on every machine, and it moves the moment a subpath starts reaching for a
module it did not need. A ratchet: a change may not grow one past the value here
without editing this file, which is the review.
`bundledBytes` is R9's own unit — esbuild --bundle --minify --format=esm, one fixture
importing one symbol — recorded rather than gated, because esbuild is not a dependency
of this package and a test that shells out to a binary it does not declare is a check
that passes for the wrong reason on the day it goes missing. `benchmarks/axes/weight.ts`
is where that measurement belongs and where the B4 row must be added; that file is the
integrator lane's, so `y8` below is recorded, not enforced. Reproduce it with the
Read `y8.holds` before quoting any of this: three of the four claims do not.

why: R9's bar is restated as D1's, and this is the restatement. Decided in the integrator
lane on 2026-09-16, on the reasoning this file already carried and the design section
§ R9 spelled out — the lane that found it could not make the change, because the bar is
one decision for the whole foundation tier and `.sdlc/bands/**` is not a package lane's
to write.
R9's own text names two things that disagree: the bar `get-east-asian-width`, and the
file `.sdlc/bands/foundation-ceilings.json`, which records D1's. D1 is the later
decision and the defensible one. `get-east-asian-width` is a width table with no
segmenter, no escape scanner and no style stack; asking six functions to weigh what one
lookup weighs was never a comparison of like with like, and four of the six foundation
layers have no zero-dependency incumbent to anchor against at all — which is the reason
D1 gives for itself.
Against D1's bar this package reads **83,536 installed bytes against a ceiling of
170,342** — the tree-inclusive bytes of `string-width`, `wrap-ansi`, `strip-ansi` and
`slice-ansi`, which is what a user removes by switching — a ratio of **0.4904**.
The old bar is kept below rather than deleted, because a bar that is restated and then
vanishes is indistinguishable from one that was quietly met. Against
`get-east-asian-width` at 3,977 bundled, one of six entries clears it: `strip.js` at
966. `index.js` is 6,180, 1.55x. That was true when it was written and it is still true.

Re-measured 2026-09-22 at 75,916 from 83,536, down 7,620 and in the same commit that made this the ninth plugin host — the two moves are unrelated and the direction is the surprise. The fall is strip-comments over a dist that grew a nested entry; the rise the plugin host adds is 1.4 KB of shared family schema, which every host pays and which D-108 records.

supersededBar.why: R9 as originally written. Recorded, not enforced — see `why` above.

perEntryRatchet: The bundled half is now gated per entry, which it never was: `benchmarks/
`benchmarks/axes/weight.ts` ratchets each at its measured value — 1.03, 1 (0.774 earns
it), 1.5 and 2.25. Those are ratchets, not claims of being lighter, and the file says so.
notBuilt: The spawn-delta clause of R9 does not apply and is not pending: this package publishes
no binary, so there is no spawn to measure. Its analogue for a library is what a
caller's bundle grows by, which is the per-entry B4 ratchet above.
